currentUse: Vacant former church and rectory at 1703 Jackson Street; the $350,000 commercial listing was marked pending as of August 11, 2026. The St. Michael the Archangel parish community (FSSP Latin Mass) that occupied it now worships at St. Lucy's Church, 949 Scranton St.

historicalNarrative.text: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish was founded in Scranton's Hyde Park neighborhood in 1914 for Lithuanian Catholics. Father Adomas Lopata served as its first pastor, and the new parish initially worshipped in a modest wooden church.

sources.locator: Vladas Būtėnas, Pennsylvanijos angliakasių Lietuva, Šv. Mykolo parapija section: 1914 founding, first pastor, and wooden church

historicalNarrative.text: Under Father Jonas Boll-Baltusevičius, the parish replaced the wooden church with the brick church on Jackson Street in 1942. The parish also maintained a school; Būtėnas recorded 205 pupils in six grades in 1961, when the parish counted about 230 families and roughly 700 people.

sources.locator: Vladas Būtėnas, Pennsylvanijos angliakasių Lietuva, Šv. Mykolo parapija section and p. 304: 1942 church and 1961 school/parish counts

historicalNarrative.text: By 1972 Saint Michael still reported 660 parishioners and 121 pupils, but Lithuanian-language life had declined sharply. In the late 1990s the parish became home to Scranton's Latin Mass community, marking a new institutional chapter while the Lithuanian-founded parish and its Jackson Street church remained in Catholic use.

profile.institutionalSummary: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish was established for Scranton's Lithuanian community in 1914. The same parish used an original wooden church, replaced it with the brick church on Jackson Street in 1942, and relocated to Saint Lucy Church in 2025. Regular Lithuanian parish life ended when the Latin Mass community assumed the parish in the late 1990s.

summary: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish survives as an FSSP Latin Mass personal parish at Saint Lucy Church, where it relocated on September 28, 2025. The former Lithuanian church and rectory at 1703 Jackson Street remain standing and vacant; their $350,000 commercial listing was marked pending as of August 11, 2026. No completed sale, buyer, or closing price is yet established. No regular Lithuanian Mass is documented at the continuing parish.

developments.headline: Final Mass at the former Lithuanian St. Michael Church; parish relocates to St. Lucy's
developments.detail: After several years of growth and increasing space needs, the St. Michael the Archangel parish community (FSSP Latin Mass personal parish) celebrated its final Mass at 1703 Jackson Street on Sept. 28, 2025, then held a Eucharistic Procession through the streets of Scranton to its new home, the historic St. Lucy Church at 949 Scranton Street. Bishop Bambera made the move as part of the Diocese of Scranton's Vision 2030 Pastoral Planning Process; pastor Fr. Anthony Dorsa, FSSP, cited the lack of classroom and gathering space at the Jackson Street site. The Jackson Street church officially closed its doors.

developments.headline: Commercial listing for former church and rectory marked pending at $350,000
developments.detail: The vacated property is listed as MLS SC261850: a 4,468 sq ft brick church built in 1942, a 2,069 sq ft rectory, and a private parking lot across the street, totaling 6,537 sq ft on 0.43 acres. The listing was marked Pending at the unchanged $350,000 asking price and showed 104 days on site when its page was last changed on August 11, 2026. Pending status does not establish a completed sale; no buyer or closing price is publicly confirmed.

developments.detail: St. Michael the Archangel Parish operates at St. Lucy's Church, 949 Scranton St., Scranton, PA 18504, with all Masses in the Traditional Latin Mass (1962 books): Sunday 8:00 am Low Mass and 10:30 am High Mass, weekday Masses Mon-Thu 7:30 am, Fri 6:00 pm, Sat 9:00 am, plus regular confessions and devotions. Pastor is Fr. Anthony Dorsa, FSSP. The parish name and community survive, but no longer in the Lithuanian-built church.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1977 published parish history resolves the earlier conflict: Saint Michael's Lithuanian parish was established in 1914, first used a modest wooden church, and replaced it with the brick church in 1942. The parish institution later survived the end of regular Lithuanian parish life, became the home of the Latin Mass community in the late 1990s, and relocated to Saint Lucy Church in 2025. The institution therefore survives, while the 1942 Lithuanian-built church is vacant and its commercial listing is pending.
gaps: The later physical disposition of the original wooden church is not established by the supplied pages. The precise date when regular Lithuanian parish life ended and the Latin Mass community assumed the parish remains bounded to the late 1990s. The $350,000 commercial listing for the 1942 Jackson Street church is marked Pending, but no completed sale, buyer, or closing price is publicly confirmed. The fate of its Lithuanian-inscribed stained glass in any future sale is unknown.
